featured_reviews.review_text:
Sunday brunch at this Rooftop Cafe was a symphony of flavors, sounds, and warmth.

The anti-pasti spread was a visual feast, with a colorful array of dips, cheeses and salads. Each bite was a masterclass in textures and flavors, with the perfect balance of tangy, spicy, sweet and savory notes. Total hit. Must try.

The refreshing mocktails were the perfect accompaniment to the meal, with unique flavor combinations that tantalized my taste buds.

The mains however could have been better. The spaghetti aglio e olio was dry and little overcooked.
The nachos were delicious.
The potato Rosti was loaded with black pepper making it difficult to eat.

The desserts were good.

The live music added a delightful ambiance with the musician's soulful voice.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a leisurely and indulgent weekend treat.

• Bombay Manchow Soup – Warm, hearty and really well prepared.
• Coke Mojito – Refreshing twist on a classic.
• Freak Shake – Indulgent and fun.

featured_reviews.name: Azim Hannure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Santosh Sagar Fast Food is a popular eatery known for its delicious, freshly prepared dishes and quick service. Located in a convenient and lively area, it attracts both locals and visitors looking for tasty and affordable meals. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including South Indian favorites like dosa, idli, and uttapam, as well as North Indian snacks, Chinese dishes, and refreshing beverages. Each item is prepared with good quality ingredients and served hot, ensuring a satisfying dining experience.

The restaurant has a clean and casual ambiance, making it perfect for families, friends, and even solo diners. The service is prompt, and the staff are friendly, polite, and attentive to customer needs. One of the highlights of Santosh Sagar Fast Food is its consistency — whether you visit for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, the taste and quality remain the same.

Prices are quite reasonable, offering great value for money, and the portion sizes are generous. It’s an excellent choice for a quick bite or a relaxed meal without compromising on flavor. Overall, Santosh Sagar Fast Food is a reliable and well-loved spot that delivers on taste, hygiene, and affordability — a true favorite among food lovers.

Review: Soam Restaurant, Mumbai

We stay in Chembur and our family visited Soam restaurant in SoBo for the first time and enjoyed a truly satisfying vegetarian dining experience.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

The service was prompt and courteous, making the meal smooth and enjoyable. The atmosphere was decent, not extraordinary, but comfortable enough for a relaxed family outing.

One point worth noting is the pricing. Compared to similar restaurants in the suburbs, Soam is on the higher side. Perhaps this is the premium for being a very popular SoBo (South Bombay) restaurant.

Overall, Soam impressed us with its authentic flavors and variety. It’s a place we would recommend to anyone looking for wholesome vegetarian food in South Mumbai, while keeping in mind the pricing.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

Thank you for sharing your detailed experience at Persian Darbar. We're delighted to hear that you enjoyed the ambience and found it to be a grand family-friendly environment. Your feedback on the food is invaluable, and we appreciate your thoughts on the dishes you tried. It’s great to know you enjoyed the Chicken Biryani!

We understand that expectations can sometimes lead to mixed experiences, and we'll take your comments about the flavors and service into consideration. Your insights help us improve and continually strive for excellence. We hope to welcome you back again in the future for an even better experience.

Thanks,
Team Persian Darbar

featured_reviews.name: Swad Stories
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Kiara Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
WAH 🚀! Just had an UNEXPECTEDLY EPIC meal at the Govinda's - didn't know food could vibe with divinity like this 🪔🍴!

🔹 *Jini Dosa*: Twisted, cheesy, and LOADED with fillings! It was like a party in my mouth 😮. The dosa was crispy, the cheese was melty... chef's touch 🧂!
🔹 *Benne Dosa*: Soft, buttery, South Indian heaven!. The benne (butter) was rich and aromatic - loved it!
🔹 *Farm Fresh Pizza*: Wait, a farm-fresh pizza inside a temple? 🤯! Toppings were fresh, crust was spot on 🍕. Got the vibe that the ingredients were picked fresh for the temple devotees... felt special!

Eating amidst the temple's vibes, felt like a foodie blessing 🙌. Service was super attentive 😊.

If you're around Iskon anywhere in the world, Govinda's is an absolute MUST 📍. Blend of divine vibes + tasty food = recipe for a soulful meal 👌."

featured_reviews.review_text:
Revival is one of those places that quietly delivers on everything you expect from a comforting dining experience. With its sea facing setting and focus on Pure Veg and Jain food, it is a spot that naturally lends itself to relaxed family outings.

A recent visit was centred around their Summer Special Mango Menu, which brings in a refreshing seasonal touch. The Kairi Kanda Roomali and Pakoda made for a great start and disappeared almost instantly. The Paneer Kairi Tikka stood out with its soft texture and well balanced flavours, easily one of the highlights from the menu.

The beverage selection complements the theme well. Options like the Mango Frozen Margarita and Mango Passion Fruit Mojito are refreshing, while the Mango Lassi is a great pick if you are in the mood for something richer and more filling.

Moving to the mains, the Paneer Khada Masala with Garlic leaves a strong impression and ranks among the better versions you will come across. It fits perfectly into the kind of comforting, flavourful food this place is known for.

Desserts keep things traditional and satisfying. The Gulab Jamun paired with Lacchedar Rabdi works beautifully, while the Aamras Puri is an easy choice, especially during the season.

What makes Revival stand out is how easy it is to return to. It is the kind of place that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for a family outing, and even welcomes your furry companions.

Conveniently located a short walk from Charni Road station, and set within a heritage building just off the Chowpatty seaface, it is a spot that is both accessible and consistently dependable when you are in the mood for good, comforting food.

When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Would not recommend until management fixes confirmed reservations, billing transparency and how they treat their customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Crystal Restaurant at Chowpatty is one of those classic places in Mumbai that has built its reputation over many years by serving consistently good food. Located close to the famous Girgaon Chowpatty, it’s a convenient spot to visit after enjoying the sea breeze or an evening walk on the beach.

The restaurant is known mainly for its simple yet delicious North Indian and vegetarian dishes. Their Punjabi thali, dal makhani, paneer preparations, and butter rotis are especially popular among regular customers. The food is rich in flavor, well-cooked, and feels like traditional home-style North Indian cuisine. Portion sizes are also quite generous, making it a good value-for-money place, especially if you’re dining with family.

One thing that stands out about Crystal is its old-school charm. The interiors are simple and not overly fancy, but the place has a warm and nostalgic feel that many longtime visitors appreciate. The staff is generally polite and efficient, and even during busy hours they try their best to serve quickly.

Another positive point is the location. Being so close to Chowpatty makes it a great stop for a proper meal after having street food or spending time by the beach. Many locals and tourists visit this restaurant when they want something more filling than snacks.

However, during peak hours the place can get quite crowded, and you might have to wait for a table. The ambiance is also more traditional than modern, so those expecting a luxury dining experience might find it a bit basic.

Overall, Crystal Restaurant is a reliable place for tasty North Indian vegetarian food in the Chowpatty area. If you’re looking for comforting meals, generous portions, and a classic Mumbai dining experience, it’s definitely worth visiting.

If you want to experience old-school Mumbai charm with soulful food and timeless vibes, then Crystal Restaurant Chowpatty is a place you simply cannot miss. Located exactly opposite Girgaon Chowpatty near Wilson College, this iconic decade-old restaurant carries the true essence of vintage Mumbai. The moment you walk in, it feels like stepping into a different era — simple interiors, retro atmosphere, classic old Hindi songs playing softly in the background, and that comforting feeling modern cafés often fail to give.
What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. Perfect spot after a long Marine Drive walk or a relaxed dinner with family and friends. The combination of Chowpatty breeze, retro Bollywood music, and homely Punjabi-style food creates an experience that feels warm and memorable.

What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vanakkam Vihar, located right opposite the iconic Royal Opera House in Girgaon, is a reliable, bustling spot for anyone craving solid, comforting South Indian comfort food in South Mumbai. Whether you are wrapping up a beach stroll at nearby Girgaon Chowpatty or stepping out after a show at the Opera House, this multi-level pure-vegetarian restaurant offers a welcoming and clean environment.
Here is a comprehensive look at what to expect:
The Vibe & Ambiance
The restaurant balances traditional charm with a modern, spacious casual-dining setup. The ground floor features comfortable high and low seating, while the upper level ("Firangi") branches out into multi-cuisine options. The space is well-lit, fully air-conditioned, and remarkably clean, making it highly family-friendly. The staff adds a touch of authenticity by dressing in traditional South Indian attire.
What to Order
While the massive menu extends to North Indian dishes and street-side snacks, the absolute highlight here remains their coastal and southern delicacies.
The Dosas: Their Kara Masala Dosa and Chettinad Dosa are beautifully crisp, served with generous portions of fresh coconut chutney, a tangy tomato-garlic chutney, and piping hot sambar. If you are looking for something lighter, the Neer Dosa and fluffy Appams paired with a rich veggie stew or Malabari curry are top-tier.
The Idli Platters: Beyond standard idlis, their Podi Idli (tossed in a vibrant, spiced gun powder and ghee) and the signature Thalaiva Idli are highly recommended.
Filter Coffee: No meal here is complete without their authentic Filter Coffee. It is served strong, perfectly frothy, and features that robust, traditional chicory-coffee blend.
Jain Options: For those with dietary restrictions, the restaurant stands out for offering a robust, dedicated selection of highly flavorful Jain South Indian variants.

Having tried authentic South Indian cuisine in Chennai and Kerala, I found Sukh Sagar’s dosa and uttapam fell short of that standard. The only dish that impressed us was the pizza.

The prices seemed quite high considering the taste and quality of the food. My mother, a senior citizen and excellent cook herself, jokingly remarked that she could prepare better food at home!

We will never come to this restaurant again.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.
